Petitioner along with other accused have been charge sheeted for the offence under Sections 120(B),
420, 465, 468, 471 of IPC, and Sections 33(A), 72 of BDA Act, and Section 321, 321(B) of Karnataka Municipalities Act, alleging that, the residential layout plan was sanctioned in favour of the Co- operative Society in question, and in the sanctioned layout plan the subject plot is earmarked as park.
created the documents purportedly to show that the plot earmarked as park was shown as plot, and thereafter was conveyed to accused No.4 in the year 2001.
Thereafter, the accused No.4, has got entered her name in the katha register, and also constructed a residential building on the subject plot after obtaining permission from the Competent Authority.

The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition by the accused No.4.
3.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that there is no allegation in the FIR or in the charge sheet that, the petitioner-accused No.4 connived with the other accused in creating the document, and in the absence of any corroborative material, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that the charge sheet material clearly discloses that, the petitioner-accused No.4 connived with the other accused in creating the documents, and the veracity of the allegations requires to be considered only after full fledged Trial, and at this stage, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate does not warrant any interference.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

6. Perusal of the FIR indicates that, the allegation of fabricating the document is only on accused No.3, who is the office bearer of the Co-operative Society, and the allegation against the petitioner-accused No.4, is that the subject plot was conveyed to her on the basis of the fabricated documents.

In the absence of any specific allegation and also in the absence of any corroborative material that, the petitioner-accused No.4 connived with the other accused in creating the documents, the charge sheet laid by the Police is without any substance and consequently, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate stands vitiated.
7.
In view of the preceding analysis, I am of the considered view that, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.4 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal petition is allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.20777/2015, on the file of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru City, insofar it relates to petitioner-accused No.4 is hereby quashed.
iii) It is made clear that, the observations made in this order is only insofar it relates to the allegations made against the petitioner-accused No.4, and the Trial Court to proceed against the other accused on the available evidence on record without being influenced by this order.
